quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'precisely' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: It is precisely this ambiguity that creates the legal problem.
quests.hint: In cleft sentences, 'precisely' intensifies the focused element before 'this'.
quests.explanation: 'Precisely' before 'this ambiguity': 'precisely this ambiguity'. In an 'it is...that' cleft, 'precisely' narrows the focus to exactly that element.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'exactly' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: That is not exactly what I meant to say.
quests.hint: Degree adverbs like 'exactly' come before the word or phrase they modify.
quests.explanation: 'Exactly' before 'what I meant': 'not exactly what I meant'. It softens the negation - the statement was close but not quite accurate.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'what' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: What she needed most was a sense of stability and belonging.
quests.hint: In subject cleft structures, 'what' fronts the clause to focus on the need.
quests.explanation: 'What she needed most' is the fronted subject: 'What she needed most was a sense of stability'. The cleft highlights the important information.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'above all' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: Above all, the approach must be fair and transparent.
quests.hint: Priority discourse markers like 'above all' front the sentence.
quests.explanation: 'Above all' opens the sentence: 'Above all, the approach must be fair'. It signals this is the most important principle.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'in turn' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: Each department submitted its report. In turn, the board reviewed them.
quests.hint: Sequence discourse markers come at the START of the clause they introduce.
quests.explanation: 'In turn' opens the second clause: 'In turn, the board reviewed them'. It signals a sequential or reciprocal relationship.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'as such' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The report contains no new evidence. As such, it cannot affect the verdict.
quests.hint: Logical consequence discourse markers come at the START of the result clause.
quests.explanation: 'As such' opens the consequence: 'As such, it cannot affect the verdict'. It means 'because of what has just been said'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'even so' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The evidence was weak. Even so, the jury returned a guilty verdict.
quests.hint: Concessive discourse markers come at the START of the contrasting clause.
quests.explanation: 'Even so' opens the contrasting clause: 'Even so, the jury returned'. It means 'despite what was just said', showing an unexpected result.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'that said' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The plan has flaws. That said, it is the best option available.
quests.hint: Concessive stance markers come at the START of the contrasting clause.
quests.explanation: 'That said' opens the qualification: 'That said, it is the best option'. It acknowledges the previous point while pivoting to a contrasting view.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'in this respect' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The two approaches differ significantly in this respect.
quests.hint: Focusing adverbials like 'in this respect' follow the main clause.
quests.explanation: 'In this respect' ends the sentence: 'differ significantly in this respect'. It specifies the dimension in which the difference applies.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'as it were' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The proposal was, as it were, a compromise between extremes.
quests.hint: Parenthetical hedging expressions are inserted with commas.
quests.explanation: 'As it were' is a parenthetical hedge: 'was, as it were, a compromise'. It signals the term is used loosely or metaphorically.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'so to speak' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: She was the glue that held the team together, so to speak.
quests.hint: Parenthetical softeners come after the idea they qualify, set off by a comma.
quests.explanation: 'So to speak' follows the main clause as a tag: 'held the team together, so to speak'. It signals the expression is figurative.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'in other words' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The merger failed. In other words, the strategy was fundamentally flawed.
quests.hint: Reformulation discourse markers come at the START of the rephrasing clause.
quests.explanation: 'In other words' opens the rephrasing: 'In other words, the strategy was flawed'. It signals a clearer restatement of the previous idea.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'at first glance' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: At first glance, the proposal looks straightforward and achievable.
quests.hint: Temporal discourse markers frame the initial impression at the START.
quests.explanation: 'At first glance' fronts the sentence: 'At first glance, the proposal looks'. It signals a preliminary impression that may change on closer inspection.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'on closer inspection' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: On closer inspection, several significant flaws become apparent.
quests.hint: Contrast discourse markers that signal a deeper look come at the START.
quests.explanation: 'On closer inspection' fronts the sentence: 'On closer inspection, several flaws become apparent'. It contrasts with a surface-level view.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'taken as a whole' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: Taken as a whole, the evidence points clearly in one direction.
quests.hint: Discourse markers signalling a holistic view front the sentence.
quests.explanation: 'Taken as a whole' fronts the sentence: 'Taken as a whole, the evidence points'. It asks the reader to consider all evidence together rather than in parts.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'from the outset' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: It was clear from the outset that the project was underfunded.
quests.hint: Time adverbials can come after 'clear' in cleft-like structures, or at the end.
quests.explanation: 'From the outset' follows 'clear': 'clear from the outset'. It specifies the timing - the problem was evident from the very beginning.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'at the expense of' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: Growth was achieved at the expense of worker welfare.
quests.hint: The prepositional phrase follows the verb and object it modifies.
quests.explanation: 'At the expense of worker welfare' follows 'achieved': 'achieved at the expense of worker welfare'. It reveals what was sacrificed for the growth.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'by and large' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: By and large, the implementation has been considered a success.
quests.hint: Summary discourse markers front the sentence to signal a general assessment.
quests.explanation: 'By and large' opens the sentence: 'By and large, the implementation has been considered a success'. It means 'generally speaking, with some exceptions'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'in retrospect' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: In retrospect, a more cautious approach would have been wiser.
quests.hint: Time-perspective discourse markers front the sentence.
quests.explanation: 'In retrospect' opens the sentence: 'In retrospect, a more cautious approach would have been wiser'. It signals reflection from a later vantage point.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'all things considered' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: All things considered, the outcome was better than expected.
quests.hint: Summary evaluative markers front the sentence to signal a balanced verdict.
quests.explanation: 'All things considered' opens the sentence: 'All things considered, the outcome was better'. It signals all factors have been weighed before the conclusion.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'needless to say' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: Needless to say, the announcement was met with considerable shock.
quests.hint: Evaluative markers signalling the obvious come at the START of the sentence.
quests.explanation: 'Needless to say' opens the sentence: 'Needless to say, the announcement was met with shock'. It signals the following point is self-evident.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'with that in mind' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: With that in mind, the committee proposed a phased implementation.
quests.hint: Forward-looking discourse markers come at the START of the consequent clause.
quests.explanation: 'With that in mind' opens the new sentence: 'With that in mind, the committee proposed'. It links the conclusion to a previous idea or consideration.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'to put it simply' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: To put it simply, the model predicts that demand will outstrip supply.
quests.hint: Reformulation markers come at the START to signal a simplified version.
quests.explanation: 'To put it simply' opens the sentence: 'To put it simply, the model predicts'. It signals the speaker will explain in plain language.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'at its core' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The debate is at its core about who bears the cost of transition.
quests.hint: Focusing phrases like 'at its core' come after the verb 'be'.
quests.explanation: 'At its core' follows 'is': 'is at its core about who bears the cost'. It identifies the fundamental nature of the debate.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'in light of' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: In light of the new evidence, the case was reopened.
quests.hint: Consequential prepositional phrases front the sentence when they motivate what follows.
quests.explanation: 'In light of the new evidence' fronts the sentence: 'In light of the new evidence, the case was reopened'. It signals the reason for the action.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'on the grounds that' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The decision was challenged on the grounds that it was unlawful.
quests.hint: Reason clauses follow the main clause.
quests.explanation: 'On the grounds that it was unlawful' follows 'challenged': 'challenged on the grounds that it was unlawful'. It states the legal basis for the challenge.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'to that end' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The committee reviewed all proposals. To that end, a subgroup was formed.
quests.hint: Purpose-consequence discourse markers come at the START of the purpose clause.
quests.explanation: 'To that end' opens the purpose clause: 'To that end, a subgroup was formed'. It means 'in order to achieve the previously stated goal'.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'without which' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: Trust is the foundation without which no partnership can succeed.
quests.hint: The relative prepositional phrase 'without which' follows the noun it modifies.
quests.explanation: 'Without which' follows 'foundation': 'the foundation without which no partnership can succeed'. The phrase adds a non-negotiable condition.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'therein' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: The regulations are complex. Therein lies the challenge for policymakers.
quests.hint: 'Therein' meaning 'in that' fronts an inverted existential sentence.
quests.explanation: 'Therein lies the challenge': 'therein' fronts the inverted sentence, placing the verb before the subject. It is a formal literary inversion.

quests.sentence: Insert the modifier 'above and beyond' into the correct position.
quests.correctAnswer: She went above and beyond what was required by the contract.
quests.hint: Idiomatic adverbial phrases follow the main verb.
quests.explanation: 'Above and beyond' follows 'went': 'went above and beyond what was required'. It means she exceeded expectations significantly.
